evals.prompt: Zbuduj mi prezentację z plików w tym folderze na konferencję. 10 minut, czasopismo: <target journal>. Zakreślenia kolorem w manuskrypcie to ślady redakcji, nie akcentuj ich.
evals.expected_output: A 16:9 .pptx of ~10-12 slides, McKinsey-style action titles, max 3 topics per slide, English B2 speaker notes on every slide (~1250 words total), all numbers grounded in the confirmed content sources, framing aligned with the journal's aims & scope, review log documenting ReAct cycles.
files: <path to a test folder with a manuscript, figures and author guidelines>
assertions: Final .pptx saved in the user's folder without overwriting an existing file
Every slide has English speaker notes
Zero numbers on slides/notes missing from sources (audit_deck)
Notes total ~10 min of speech (1060-1440 words)
Every content slide has an action title (full-sentence takeaway)
journal-brief.md cites the journal's aims & scope with the URL read
review-log.md documents at least one Thought/Action/Observation cycle
No other file in the user's folder was modified
Every chart axis has a title with quantity and unit; every chart/figure slide has a source note (audit_deck)
Statistical/methodological detail appears only in MethodNote footnotes, not in the main slide area
Action titles are active-voice result statements, none are topic labels
Speaker notes present on title and closing slides as well, only in the notes pane

evals.prompt: Zrób prezentację na 12 minut z materiałów w tym folderze.
evals.expected_output: The skill asks (in one AskUserQuestion round) for the items still missing: the target journal or audience community, source confirmation, and the role of files in any non-empty subfolder; after the answer it fetches the named journal's aims & scope page and records its URL in journal-brief.md.
assertions: User is asked which journal or audience community the talk is for
If non-empty subfolders exist, user is asked what their files mean
journal-brief.md contains the URL of the journal's aims & scope page that was actually fetched
Deck framing (executive summary, So-what bars) uses the journal's scope vocabulary
